signatures.name: External Secrets cannot fetch a value from the secret store
signatures.pattern: "msg":"Reconciler error"(?!.*Operation cannot be fulfilled).*"controller":"externalsecret"|"controller":"externalsecret"(?!.*Operation cannot be fulfilled).*"msg":"Reconciler error"|could not get secret data from provider|unable to create session|Secret does not exist
signatures.meaning: The ExternalSecret has SecretSynced=False. New pods use the old Secret, or there is no Secret at all and they fail to start. The line is controller-runtime's Reconciler error for the externalsecret controller (every version; the provider error is in its "error" field), plus the operator's own `could not get secret data from provider` line that only versions up to 0.10.0 print. Both signatures of this collector count the Reconciler error line; this one adds the AWS session and missing-secret texts.
signatures.cause: IRSA role permissions, secret renamed or deleted, region mismatch, expired token.

signatures.name: Karpenter does not support the cluster Kubernetes version
signatures.pattern: failed validating kubernetes version|validating kubernetes version, karpenter( version)? is not compatible with (K8s|kubernetes) version
signatures.meaning: The Karpenter controller considers the EKS Kubernetes version outside its supported range (MinK8sVersion..MaxK8sVersion of the provider). Up to v1.0.x this is the "failed validating kubernetes version" error line; from v1.1.0 it is the error field of the version controller's "Reconciler error". The nodeclass.status controller stops resolving AMIs, so new nodes do not launch or launch only with old AMIs.
signatures.cause: EKS was upgraded without upgrading the Karpenter chart (or vice versa), or 1.x version validation is on and the patch version is outside the support table.
signatures.verify: kubectl logs -n karpenter -l app.kubernetes.io/name=karpenter --since=24h | grep -c 'validating kubernetes version'; helm list -n karpenter

signatures.name: EBS CSI cannot find the VolumeSnapshot CRD (snapshot controller not installed)
signatures.pattern: failed to list \*v1\.VolumeSnapshot(Class|Content)?: the server could not find the requested resource
signatures.meaning: external-snapshotter (CRD + snapshot-controller) is missing, so VolumeSnapshots cannot be created. Velero/CSI snapshot backups are impossible and the csi-snapshotter sidecar logs the reflector error on every list retry (two lines per retry with client-go 0.31, one with 0.37).
signatures.cause: Only the EBS CSI add-on was installed, without the snapshot-controller (separate add-on or kubernetes-csi/external-snapshotter).
signatures.verify: kubectl get crd volumesnapshotclasses.snapshot.storage.k8s.io; kubectl get deploy -n kube-system snapshot-controller

signatures.name: metrics-server cannot scrape node kubelets
signatures.meaning: The CPU/memory metrics HPAs use are missing or stale. HPAs stall at "unknown". "Failed to scrape node" is the E line (klog V0) with the kubelet client error in err=; x509 and certificate match Go's TLS verification errors inside that value.
signatures.cause: kubelet serving certificate verification failure (environments needing --kubelet-insecure-tls), network policy, node NotReady.
signatures.verify: kubectl top nodes; kubectl get apiservice v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io

signatures.name: Spot or capacity-reservation interruption notice
signatures.meaning: EC2 announced it will reclaim a spot node in 2 minutes and Karpenter deleted the NodeClaim ("initiating delete from interruption message" with messageKind spot_interrupted, SpotInterruptionKind on 0.37.x). Its pods get rescheduled. If frequent, widen the spot pool selection. Rebalance recommendations are Events only.
signatures.cause: Spot market fluctuation. The narrower the instance types, the more frequent.
